- If sentiment is consistently low (≤0.11) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward slightly.
- If model shows sharp upward spikes (e.g., >73) followed by high sentiment, often overcorrects; cap or reduce peak forecasts.
- When true outcome is significantly higher than recent 10-day average, model often lags; add 1–2% buffer to forecast for such periods.
- If sentiment is rising (≥0.17) and model is flat or declining, model underreacts; increase forecast slope or magnitude.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome deviates >5% from 14-day moving average, apply mean reversion correction toward prior trend.
- If model forecast is consistently 2–3% below true outcome over 3–5 consecutive days, add 0.5–1.0% to next forecast to compensate for persistent underestimation.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.17) and model is overpredicting, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% to avoid overshoot.
